issues.legal_issue: The right to life includes the right to livelihood, and an eviction that puts that right in jeopardy may violate constitutional protections.
material_facts: The petitions challenged the eviction of slum and pavement dwellers under state laws governing slums, public-land encroachments, municipal streets and town planning.
The petitioners sought protection from eviction without alternative accommodation and sought basic amenities for slum dwellers.
The Court held that the constitutional points decided in the pavement- and slum-dweller cases concerning Bombay governed these petitions.
issues.conclusion: The right to life under Article 21 includes the right to livelihood because a person cannot live without the means of living. An eviction that puts that right in jeopardy is violative of Articles 21 and 19(1)(e) and (g).
issues.legal_principle: Article 21 protects more than mere physical existence: the right to livelihood is an integral component of the right to life. The Court applied Olga Tellis & Ors. v. Bombay Municipal Corporation & Ors. and applied the constitutional ruling to eviction under the Tamil Nadu Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1971, read with the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905, the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919, and the Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act, 1971. The judgment also describes Section 11(a) of the 1971 Slum Areas Act as providing for a slum-clearance declaration after the specified opportunity for landowners to show cause.

predicates.eviction_challenge: A person brings a proceeding challenging eviction from a slum or pavement.
predicates.livelihood_at_stake: The eviction deprives the affected person of the means of livelihood and thereby puts the person's ability to live in jeopardy.

issues.definition: When an eviction is challenged and it puts the affected person's livelihood at stake, the eviction violates the constitutional rights described in the ruling.

issues.legal_issue: A court need not issue a general mandamus requiring alternative accommodation before every eviction or directing basic amenities when the government is pursuing an improvement and rehabilitation policy and the record supports that it is being implemented.
material_facts: The petitioners sought a general restraint on evicting slum and pavement dwellers without alternative accommodation and an order requiring water, drainage and electricity for slum dwellers.
The State's affidavits described measures to improve slums, provide amenities and offer alternative accommodation where slums could not be improved.

The Court was satisfied from the affidavits that the State had adopted a benevolent policy, was taking steps to improve slums and provided alternative accommodation before evicting residents from slums that could not be improved.
The State gave an assurance that residents of slums who had been living there before the policy cutoff would not be evicted without alternative accommodation.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to issue the requested general writ or direction, but held the State to its assurance and issued specific protections concerning eviction.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the need for general writ relief in light of the government's stated policy and the evidence that it was being carried out. It treated the government's assurance concerning qualifying slum residents as binding. No separate statutory test for granting the requested general mandamus is stated in the judgment.

rule.if: writ_proceeding and broad_eviction_or_amenities_relief_sought and government_rehabilitation_policy and policy_implementation_supported

predicates.writ_proceeding: A person brings a writ proceeding seeking court-ordered protection or services for slum or pavement dwellers.
predicates.broad_eviction_or_amenities_relief_sough: The proceeding seeks general protection from eviction without alternative accommodation, basic amenities, or both.
predicates.government_rehabilitation_policy: The government states that it is improving slums and providing alternative accommodation where improvement is not possible.
predicates.policy_implementation_supported: The record supports the court's finding that the government is taking steps to implement its stated improvement and rehabilitation policy.

issues.definition: When a writ proceeding seeks broad eviction or amenities relief and the government's rehabilitation policy is supported by evidence of implementation, the court need not issue a general mandamus.

issues.legal_issue: Specific protections against eviction may be ordered for pavement and slum dwellers according to their residence category, eligibility under the government's cutoff policy, and the urgency of the public need for the land.
material_facts: The petitions concerned both pavement dwellers and slum dwellers facing eviction.
The State had adopted a cutoff for identifying residents eligible for alternative accommodation and assured the Court that qualifying slum dwellers would not be evicted without it.
The Court ordered a temporary bar on evicting pavement dwellers and most other slum dwellers, subject to the stated exception for an urgent public purpose.

The Court directed the State to do its best to provide alternative accommodation to pavement dwellers who could establish qualifying residence, and held the State to its assurance for qualifying slum dwellers.
issues.conclusion: Pavement dwellers were not to be evicted before the specified temporary deadline, and the State was to do its best to provide alternative accommodation to qualifying residents. Qualifying slum dwellers were not to be evicted without alternative accommodation. Other slum dwellers were not to be evicted before that deadline unless the land was required for an urgent public purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the constitutional protections governing livelihood and relied on the State's assurance as binding for qualifying slum dwellers. It tailored relief to the affected groups: temporary protection for pavement dwellers and other slum dwellers, alternative-accommodation protection for qualifying residents, and an exception for an urgent public purpose in the case of other slum dwellers.

rule.if: writ_proceeding and (pavement_dweller or (slum_dweller and (eligible_under_cutoff_policy or not urgent_public_need)))

predicates.writ_proceeding: A person brings a writ proceeding concerning the eviction of pavement or slum dwellers.
predicates.pavement_dweller: The person affected by the eviction lives on a pavement.
predicates.slum_dweller: The person affected by the eviction lives in a slum.
predicates.eligible_under_cutoff_policy: The person's residence falls within the category covered by the government's cutoff-based assurance or accommodation effort.
predicates.urgent_public_need: The government requires the land on which the slum stands for an urgent public purpose.

issues.definition: The rule protects pavement dwellers and protects slum dwellers who qualify under the government's policy or whose land is not urgently required for a public purpose.
